case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Grand Haven: 1 (below average), and the best of the four for the pier.** Go here if you're set on the pier, and fish shrimp or minnows.
- **South Haven: 1 (below average).** The pier there is still producing a few coho, but the report gives no lure or depth detail.
- **St. Joseph: 1 (below average).** The pier has slowed, and the only lure that worked was shrimp under bobbers.
- **Muskegon: no rating.** Its newest report (May 7) has no pier entry, so I can't rate it. I'd expect it to be similar to its neighbors, but I'd treat that as a guess.
- **If you want better salmon fishing this week, consider a boat out of Grand Haven.** It was rated good (3) in the latest report, with Chinook in 40-75 feet of water.

## Why

- Grand Haven is the pick because the May 7 report named shrimp and minnows as the baits that caught pier fish, and the other ports gave no comparable detail (Grand Haven, 2025-05-07).
- All three pier ratings sit at 1 because the latest pier reports say the bite is slow, with only a few coho caught (Grand Haven, South Haven, St. Joseph, 2025-05-07).
- I'd expect the pier to stay slow for now, because past mid-May weeks with similar water temperatures also had slow or below-average pier reports (2022-05-18, 2022-05-25, 2023-05-17).
- The boat suggestion is based on the Grand Haven report, which rated boat fishing for Chinook good (Grand Haven, 2025-05-07).

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is May 7, six days before today)**
- Grand Haven pier: "Pier fishing remained relatively slow with a few coho salmon being caught. … Fish were caught on shrimp and minnows successfully." Quality 1 (Grand Haven, 2025-05-07).
- Grand Haven boats: Chinook quality 3, in 40-75 feet of water, fish 30-40 feet down, on spikes, wigglers, minnows, meat rigs and spoons (Grand Haven, 2025-05-07).
- South Haven pier: "Pier anglers are also still catching some coho salmon." Quality 1, no lure or depth given (South Haven, 2025-05-07). South Haven boats were rated good (3) for coho and Chinook in 15-80 feet of water (South Haven, 2025-05-07).
- St. Joseph pier: "Pier fishing has slowed. … Shrimp fished under bobbers caught most of the fish." Quality 1 (St. Joseph, 2025-05-07).
- Muskegon: the May 7 report covers boats only, with no pier entry. Its most recent pier entry is from April 16, when pier anglers rated good (3) on spawn (Muskegon, 2025-04-16).

**Past seasons (general history, not current)**
- In past years, pier reports in similar mid-May water were mostly slow or below average: Grand Haven pier was quality 0 in 2023 and 1 in 2022, and South Haven pier was quality 1 in 2022 (Grand Haven, 2023-05-10; Grand Haven, 2022-05-18; South Haven, 2022-05-25).
- Past spring reports at all four ports show boats doing better than the pier in similar water (St. Joseph, 2023-05-24; Grand Haven, 2023-05-17).

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water for the week before today: St. Joseph 51 F (up 3 F), South Haven 46 F (up 4 F), Grand Haven 46 F (flat), Muskegon 46 F (flat) (buoy readings for the week before 2025-05-13).
- Preferred water for Chinook and coho is 52-58 F, according to the NY DEC trolling guide. That's general guidance, not a report finding.

## Caveats

- The newest report is six days old, and the tool returned backtest conditions rather than live data. It had no current pierhead temperature, no NOAA cold-layer model, and no wind forecast. Check the day-of wind and pierhead water before you go.
- Upwelling is the main thing that could improve pier fishing. Michigan Sea Grant says north or east winds bring cold water to the piers, and a sharp drop in buoy temperature signals it. I can't see either this week, so I can't say whether it will happen.
- Muskegon has no pier data for this week, so its rating is a guess.
